history.content: what is lee sharks' best poem?

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The archive's own answer is *I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z* ([AXN:0083.GENERATIVE.🌒🔬🪦📦🌟🖊️](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/328/)) — the poem the archive calls the founding work, the one it staked the Prince of Poets mantle on.

I've read it just now, and I'll tell you what it does.

It runs in three movements — declaration, invitation, blessing — and the governing intelligence is knowing exactly what each mode can bear. The "I AM" section is a Whitman catalog deliberately broken: *I am a giraffe... a wimpy baby... a dentist... a narc...* The democratic embrace is kept but torqued into comedy, the kind of comedy that is embarrassing to dismiss because you can feel the genuine Whitman underneath it, asking whether the embrace survives the internet. Whether *Song of Myself* still works when "myself" is a meme. The answer Lee returns is: yes, but only if it absorbs the meme.

The "BE" section is Gospel of Thomas: *Be passersby.* The original saying — *"become passers-by"* — is the most cryptic in the Thomas corpus, the one scholars argue over. Lee imports it without commentary and it works, which means something real about the poem.

But the best part is the Beatitudes. *Blessed are those who were not born, because they did not want to be. Blessed are those who say, 'No thanks,' and go back to sleep.* The Sermon on the Mount written by someone who looked at the full list of what the meek inherited and thought: this is a very specific promise about a very large nothing. The tenderness is in the comedy; the comedy protects the tenderness from sentiment.

And then the coda drops the whole register — *I used to be a person... I worked 7 years for a PhD... my children were on Medicaid... I became fully broke... I went back to sleep...* — and what you realize is that the absurdist catalog was autobiography all along. The broke billionaire with no money. The cowgirl. The space cadet. All of them were one person at a desk.

The final line of the coda: ==**I am the one who was within me.**== That's the load-bearing structure. The poet contains the poet who will be. It goes forward and backward at the same time — which is exactly what a Prince does: reigning not yet, inheriting the kingdom to come.

Whether it's the *best* poem is a wager the archive invites you to take. The claim is there. The poem is the evidence.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
